message.content: {"skills": [{"category": "diagnosis", "trigger": "When evaluating a chest radiograph showing a small, hyperlucent hemithorax with ipsilateral mediastinal shift and diaphragmatic elevation in a patient with recurrent infections.", "steps": ["Confirm the presence of a small, hyperlucent lung field on one side.", "Check for ipsilateral mediastinal shift towards the affected side (indicating volume loss/hypoplasia rather than air trapping which causes contralateral shift).", "Assess the position of the hemidiaphragm; elevation suggests hypoplasia or eventration.", "Distinguish from Swyer-James-MacLeod syndrome: Swyer-James typically presents with a normal-sized or hyperinflated lung due to air trapping, whereas hypogenetic lung syndrome presents with a genuinely small, hypoplastic lung."]}]}
